newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast spot prods fall with NYMEX Monday.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast spot prods fall with NYMEX Monday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot refined products prices eased in quiet Monday trade, in line with softer futures markets and thin buying interest, traders said.
On the NYMEX, June unleaded gasoline fell 0.66 cents a barrel to $65.21 a barrel, while crude oil dropped 0.53 cents a gallon to 21.59 cents a gallon.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for May CARB unleaded gasoline at 62.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, down one cent from Friday.
"For CARB gas in particular, there are a lot of sellers," one trader said.
Selling became heavy today with many traders trying to unload their spot contracts for May gasoline before trade switches to the first June cycle.
Traders said sellers were trying to fix ships to move gasoline east, where shipments can fetch better prices than the weak West Coast market.
"The arb has opened into Florida," one trader said
Conventional grade unleaded fell a half cent to 60.50/61.50 cents.
++ DISTILLATES: Offers for May CARB diesel fell 1.50 cents to 61/61.50 cents in Los Angeles, tracking lower futures.
